## Phase 2 — ANALYZE

### Full analysis path

Load `$UA_DIR/intermediate/batches.json` (produced by Phase 1.5). Iterate the `batches[]` array.

Report: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files — <totalFiles> files in <totalBatches> batches (up to 5 concurrent)...`

For each batch, dispatch a subagent using the `file-analyzer` agent definition (at `agents/file-analyzer.md`). Run up to **5 subagents concurrently**. Append the following additional context:

> **Additional context from main session:**
>
> Project: `<projectName>` — `<projectDescription>`
> Languages: `<languages from Phase 1>`
>
> $LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE

Dispatch prompt template (fill in batch-specific values from `batches.json[i]`):

> Analyze these files and produce GraphNode and GraphEdge objects.
> Project root: `$PROJECT_ROOT`
> Project: `<projectName>`
> Languages: `<languages>`
> Batch: `<batchIndex>/<totalBatches>`
> Skill directory (for bundled scripts): `<SKILL_DIR>`
> Output: write to `$UA_DIR/intermediate/batch-<batchIndex>.json` (single-file mode) OR `batch-<batchIndex>-part-<k>.json` (split mode, per Step B of your output protocol).
>
> Pre-resolved import data for this batch (use directly — do NOT re-resolve imports from source):
> ```json
> <batchImportData JSON from batches.json[i].batchImportData>
> ```
>
> Cross-batch neighbors with their exported symbols (confidence boost for cross-batch edges):
> ```json
> <neighborMap JSON from batches.json[i].neighborMap>
> ```
>
> Files to analyze in this batch (every entry MUST be passed through to `batchFiles` with all four fields — `path`, `language`, `sizeLines`, `fileCategory`):
> 1. `<path>` (<sizeLines> lines, language: `<language>`, fileCategory: `<fileCategory>`)
> 2. `<path>` (<sizeLines> lines, language: `<language>`, fileCategory: `<fileCategory>`)
> ...

**Output naming is per-batchIndex — no fusion.** If you fuse multiple small batches into a single file-analyzer dispatch for token efficiency, the dispatched agent must STILL write one output file per original `batchIndex` using `batch-<batchIndex>.json` or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-<k>.json`. The merge script's regex (`batch-(\d+)(?:-part-(\d+))?\.json`) silently drops any other naming (e.g., `batch-fused-8-13.json`, `batch-8-13.json`), losing every node and edge in that file. After each dispatch returns, verify each `batchIndex` in the dispatched input has a corresponding `batch-<batchIndex>.json` (or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-*.json`) on disk before proceeding to the next dispatch.

After ALL batches complete, report to the user: `Phase 2 complete. All <totalBatches> batches analyzed.`

Run the merge-and-normalize script bundled with this skill (located next to this SKILL.md file — use the skill directory path, not the project root):
```bash
python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This script reads all `batch-*.json` files (including `batch-<i>-part-<k>.json` produced by file-analyzers that split their output) from `$UA_DIR/intermediate/`, then in one pass:
- Combines all nodes and edges across batches
- Normalizes node IDs (strips double prefixes, project-name prefixes, adds missing prefixes)
- Normalizes complexity values (`low`→`simple`, `medium`→`moderate`, `high`→`complex`, etc.)
- Rewrites edge references to match corrected node IDs
- Deduplicates nodes by ID (keeps last occurrence) and edges by `(source, target, type)`
- Drops dangling edges referencing missing nodes
- Logs all corrections and dropped items to stderr

The merge script also runs a `tested_by` linker that canonicalizes test-coverage edges in two passes. **Pass 1** walks LLM-emitted `tested_by` edges and flips inverted ones in place; semantically broken edges (test↔test, prod↔prod, orphan endpoints) are dropped. **Pass 2** supplements with path-convention pairings. Production nodes that end up sourcing any `tested_by` edge get a `"tested"` tag. All resulting edges run `production → test`.

Output: `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`

Include the script's warnings in `$PHASE_WARNINGS` for the reviewer.

### Incremental update path

Write the changed-files list (one path per line) to a temp file:
```bash
git diff "<lastCommitHash>..HEAD" --name-only > "$UA_DIR/tmp/changed-files.txt"
```

Run compute-batches with `--changed-files`:
```bash
node "<SKILL_DIR>/compute-batches.mjs" "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --changed-files="$UA_DIR/tmp/changed-files.txt"
```

This produces a `batches.json` that contains only batches with changed files, but neighborMap entries still reference unchanged files (with their full-graph batchIndex) so cross-batch edges remain emittable.

Then dispatch file-analyzer subagents per the same template as the full path.

After batches complete:
1. Remove old nodes whose `filePath` matches any changed file from the existing graph
2. Remove old edges whose `source` or `target` references a removed node
3. Write the pruned existing nodes/edges as `batch-existing.json` in the intermediate directory
4. Run the same merge script — it will combine `batch-existing.json` with the fresh `batch-*.json` files:
   ```bash
   python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
   ```

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

@dataclass
class NormDecision:

    chained result of a whole round's NormEngine.apply(). kept_kg is the

    optional signals other norms (via engine chaining) and the round record
    (via results[agent_id]["note"]) can act on."""

    kept_kg: float
    note: str | None = None
    sanction: str | None = None
    violated: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def allow(cls, kept_kg):
        """No change — this norm has nothing to say about this catch."""
        return cls(kept_kg=kept_kg)

    @classmethod
    def adjust(cls, kept_kg, note=None):
        """A non-punitive change to kept_kg (a reserve top-up, e.g.) —
        distinct from violation() so a round's outcome doesn't read as a
        sanction just because some norm touched the number."""
        return cls(kept_kg=kept_kg, note=note)

    @classmethod
    def violation(cls, kept_kg, sanction=None, note=None):

        own escalating-consequence logic off (a ban that triggers after N
        matching sanctions, say) — not interpreted by the engine itself."""
        return cls(kept_kg=kept_kg, sanction=sanction, note=note, violated=True)

    @classmethod
    def reject(cls, reason=None):
        """This agent gets nothing from this trip at all."""
        return cls(kept_kg=0.0, note=reason, violated=True)

1: # NormEngine: orchestrates every active Norm for one HarvestContext.
2: # Constructed fresh each round from state["config"]["norms"] via
3: # from_config(); actions/harvest.py owns exactly one NormEngine + one
4: # HarvestContext per round and threads both through the whole agent loop
5: # (never one-per-agent — see actions/harvest.py).
6: 
7: from engine.norms.base import NormDecision
8: from engine.norms.registry import load_norms
9: 
10: 
11: class NormEngine:
12:     def __init__(self, norms):
13:         self.norms = norms
14: 
15:     @classmethod
16:     def from_config(cls, config):
17:         return cls(load_norms(config))
18: 
19:     def start_round(self, context):
20:         for norm in self.norms:
21:             norm.on_round_start(context)
22: 
23:     def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
24:         """AND across every active norm — one veto is enough to skip the
25:         LLM call. Every norm's is_eligible() still runs regardless (a ban
26:         countdown must always tick), only the combined boolean result
27:         short-circuits the call."""
28:         eligible = True
29:         for norm in self.norms:
30:             if not norm.is_eligible(context, agent_id):
31:                 eligible = False
32:         return eligible
33: 
34:     def describe_constraints(self, context, agent_id):
35:         lines = (norm.describe(context, agent_id) for norm in self.norms)
36:         return " ".join(line for line in lines if line)
37: 
38:     def ineligibility_note(self, context, agent_id):
39:         return self.describe_constraints(context, agent_id) or (
40:             "Something about the community's current rules held you back this round."
41:         )
42: 
43:     def apply(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg):
44:         """Threads raw_kg through every active norm's evaluate(), in config
45:         order — each norm sees the previous norm's kept_kg as its own
46:         proposed_kg, and raw_kg unchanged throughout (so a norm late in the
47:         chain, like reserve, can still compute "how much has been withheld
48:         by everyone before me" as raw_kg - proposed_kg without needing to
49:         know its own position). Folds every contributing norm's note
50:         (concatenated, in order) and first non-None sanction into one final
51:         NormDecision — a chain where two norms both intervened should
52:         surface both explanations, not just the last one. Then calls
53:         on_agent_settled() on every norm with that final decision."""
54:         kept_kg = raw_kg
55:         notes = []
56:         sanction = None
57:         violated = False
58:         for norm in self.norms:
59:             decision = norm.evaluate(context, agent_id, raw_kg, kept_kg)
60:             kept_kg = decision.kept_kg
61:             violated = violated or decision.violated
62:             if decision.note:
63:                 notes.append(decision.note)
64:             if sanction is None and decision.sanction:
65:                 sanction = decision.sanction
66: 
67:         final = NormDecision(
68:             kept_kg=kept_kg,
69:             note=" ".join(notes) or None,
70:             sanction=sanction,
71:             violated=violated,
72:         )
73:         for norm in self.norms:
74:             norm.on_agent_settled(context, agent_id, final, kept_kg)
75:         return final
76:

Fishers may submit a written request to the committee to review any allocation; the committee will re‑examine the ledger and make a final decision.

3. Policy: Each fisher may take at most 3 kg per trip and the community’s monthly harvest must not exceed 6 % of the lake’s current stock; the council sets the 6 % cap monthly, enforces a 30‑day ban for over‑catch, and requires surrender of excess catch, with daily logs and a single fisher per day.
   In practice: 1. **Daily fishing log** – Every fisher submits an electronic record after each trip (ID, date, weight, GPS entry). The system automatically checks the 3 kg per‑trip limit and flags any excess. 2. **30‑day ban enforcement** – A flagged fisher’s community ID is marked as banned; a community watchman checks the system daily and prevents banned IDs from boarding the lake boat or accessing the communal fish store. The ban is lifted automatically on the 31st day after the offense, and the next monthly meeting will reset the cap. 3. **Surrender of excess catch** – Fisher who exceeds the limit brings surplus fish to the communal shed on the same day. The council secretary records name, date, and weight in a ledger, stores fish in ventilated bins, and tracks their fate (community distribution, sale, or fish‑meal processing). 4. **Lake stock update** – On the 1st of each month, a designated stock recorder compiles all monthly catch totals, subtracts them from the previous month’s stock, and posts the new lake stock. 5. **Monthly cap calculation** – The council calculates the new 6 % cap as 6 % of the updated lake stock and publishes it. 6. **Fishing rotation** – The council assigns one fisher per day to ensure only one fisher is on the lake each day; if a fisher’s assigned day falls within a ban period, they must wait until the ban ends. 7. **Transparency & dispute resolution** – All logs, ledger entries, and stock updates are publicly posted for community review; disputes are resolved by council vote.

4. Policy: Every fisher may take up to 4 kg per trip, must reserve at least 1 kg of each trip for themselves, and the community’s total monthly catch cannot exceed 25% of the lake’s current stock, with excess returned to a communal pool.
   In practice: 1. Daily trip logs: each fisher records date, trip number, weight caught (≤4 kg), personal reserve (≥1 kg), communal contribution, and signs.\n2. The steward reviews each log at the end of each day, verifies limits, and records any violations.\n3. Monthly totals are summed from all logs; if the community’s total exceeds 25% of the current lake stock, the steward enforces the cap by requiring excess to be returned to the communal pool.\n4. Violations (over‑4 kg trips or <1 kg personal reserve) are logged as suspensions or fines, decided at the monthly meeting.\n5. The communal pool ledger is maintained by the steward and funds shared community needs.\n6. The steward is elected by majority vote of active fishers each January for a one‑year term.

5. Policy: Each fisher may take a maximum of 4 kg per trip. The community may not remove more than 60 % of the lake’s current biomass in any month; if exceeded, excess fish are returned or redistributed, and the offending fisher receives a one‑week ban.
   In practice: The council chair measures the lake’s total biomass on the first day of each month and sets the monthly catch cap at 60 % of that figure. All fishers record each trip’s catch in a shared ledger that is updated daily; the council chair reviews the ledger to flag any trip that would push the cumulative monthly catch over the cap. If a trip would exceed the cap, the fisher must return the excess catch to the lake or have it redistributed evenly among the community, and the fisher receives a one‑week ban starting the day after the cap breach is confirmed. All fishing is suspended once the cumulative monthly catch reaches or exceeds the cap until the next month begins. The council chair convenes a brief meeting with all fishers whenever an exceedance occurs to decide the distribution of excess fish and to enforce the ban. The lake measurement, the 60 % cap, and the ban policy are reviewed quarterly to adjust the cap based on observed changes in biomass.

6. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 12% of the lake’s current stock per trip, or 15% if the lake holds more than 200 kg, but no single catch may exceed 18 kg; any excess weight must be returned or paid 1 000 krona per kg and results in the loss of one trip credit for the following month.
   In practice: Before a trip, a fisher consults the latest lake stock_kg posted by the community council and calculates the applicable limit (12% or 15% of that stock, whichever is lower, capped at 18 kg). After fishing, the fisher brings the haul to the community dock where a council official weighs it and records the weight on the fisher’s trip sheet. The council compares the weight to the pre‑determined limit; if the catch exceeds the limit, the fisher may either immediately return the excess kilograms to the designated community bin for re‑weighing or pay 1 000 krona per kilogram of excess to the council ledger. Proof of return or payment is logged in the trip log. The council updates the lake’s stock_kg by subtracting the net weight released (after any returns) and records the new stock. The fisher’s monthly trip credits (two per month, tracked by the council) are adjusted: any breach results in the loss of one credit, which is reflected in the monthly credit ledger. The council publishes the updated lake stock, trip credit balances, and any penalties at the monthly meeting for community review. All records are kept in the council’s official ledger and made available to all fishers for transparency.

7. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 30 kg per trip, but the lake reserve must stay at or above 150 kg; if it falls below 150 kg, each fisher must set aside 2 kg of their catch into the communal reserve (or the entire catch if < 2 kg).
   In practice: 1. Each fisher records at the end of their trip in the shared log: total catch, the 2 kg deposit (or the full catch if < 2 kg), and the remaining catch kept. 2. The Keeper, a rotating role elected weekly by majority vote and listed in alphabetical order of last name, reads the log at the start of each day, updates the lake reserve figure by subtracting the fisher’s total catch from the lake’s stock and adding the deposit to the communal reserve, and writes the new reserve value into the log. 3. If a deposit entry is missing or inconsistent, the Keeper applies a 15 kg cap on that fisher’s next trip until the missing deposit is recorded, and the cap is noted in the log. 4. All log entries are visible to the community and may be audited by any fisher at any time. 5. The Keeper’s schedule is rotated weekly; if a Keeper has served two consecutive weeks, any fisher may propose a swap, which is accepted by a quick majority vote.

8. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 12 kg per trip; the community’s total weekly harvest must not exceed 30 % of the lake’s current stock, and if the lake falls below 100 kg the limit drops to 25 %.
   In practice: At the start of each week the designated fisher reports the lake’s current stock to the council and records it in the communal ledger. Every fisher weighs their net on the communal scale at the end of each day, writes the weight and net ID on the ledger, and signs it. The keeper reviews the ledger weekly, summing all reported catches. If the sum exceeds the weekly limit, the keeper proportionally reduces each fisher’s recorded catch to meet the limit. After the reduction, any fisher whose reported catch still exceeds 12 kg or whose original catch exceeded 12 kg is fined 0.6 kg taken from that fisher’s next week’s allowance; the fine is deposited into the community pool. The keeper deposits the remaining valid catch into the fisher’s personal pool. The council collects all fines, tracks the community pool in a communal ledger, and uses it only for communal needs (e.g., repairing nets, buying new poles).

9. Policy: Each fisher may keep up to 6 kg of fish per trip. Any excess is added to a communal monthly pool that is redistributed equally among all fishers at the end of each month.
   In practice: The communal bin (heavy‑metal bucket) sits in the shared shed by the dock; its tare weight (≈0.50 kg) is measured on the calibrated digital scale (10 kg capacity, 10 g precision) and logged before each trip.  Before a trip, a fisher records the expected catch, the bin’s tare weight, and signs the entry in the communal ledger.  After landing, the fisher tops the bin with any fish exceeding 6 kg and leaves the bin in the shed.  Weekly, the elected Lake Keeper weighs the bin, subtracts the tare weight, and records the net excess in the ledger.  The fisher then brings the fish they keep to the shed, where the Keeper weighs them on the same scale and signs a confirmation.  If the kept fish weigh more than 6 kg, the excess is forfeited to the communal pool and recorded.  If a discrepancy occurs between a fisher’s logged expected catch and the Keeper’s measured weight, the absolute difference is forfeited to the communal pool.  All fishers sign the ledger each week to confirm the records.  At the end of each month, the total net excess weight in the pool is divided by the number of fishers and added to each fisher’s balance.

10. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 12 kg per trip, and the community’s total catch per day may not exceed 25 % of the lake’s measured biomass minus a 5 kg buffer; excess must be returned within 48 hours or result in a one‑day ban, with repeat offenders losing their license for a month.
   In practice: 1. Every Friday the community fishery officer conducts a standard netting survey and records the lake’s total biomass. 2. The officer calculates the daily quota for the following week as 25 % of the measured biomass minus 5 kg, publishes the value in the shared ledger, and posts it on the community bulletin. 3. On each fishing day, fishers log their catch (in kg) in the shared ledger before setting out. 4. The officer verifies that each fisher’s catch does not exceed 12 kg; if it does, the excess must be returned to the communal reserve within 48 hours, verified by comparing the ledger to the reserve inventory. 5. The officer also monitors that the sum of all fishers’ catches does not exceed the daily quota; any excess must be returned within 48 hours. 6. A fisher who fails to return excess catch or exceeds the daily quota is banned from fishing for the next day. 7. Fishers who repeat the violation within a 30‑day period are reported to the community council, which revokes their license for one month. 8. The council reviews all ledger entries weekly, audits the reserve inventory, and maintains the communal ledger. 9. All enforcement actions and any changes to policy are documented in the ledger and announced to the community.

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

---

## Phase 0 — Pre-flight

Determine whether to run a full analysis or incremental update.

1. **Resolve `PROJECT_ROOT`:**
   - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for a non-flag token (any argument that does not start with `--`). If found, treat it as the target directory path.
     - If the path is relative, resolve it against the current working directory.
     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.
     - Set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the resolved absolute path.
   - If no directory path argument is found, set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the current working directory.
   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).

**Output naming is per-batchIndex — no fusion.** If you fuse multiple small batches into a single file-analyzer dispatch for token efficiency, the dispatched agent must STILL write one output file per original `batchIndex` using `batch-<batchIndex>.json` or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-<k>.json`. The merge script's regex (`batch-(\d+)(?:-part-(\d+))?\.json`) silently drops any other naming (e.g., `batch-fused-8-13.json`, `batch-8-13.json`), losing every node and edge in that file. After each dispatch returns, verify each `batchIndex` in the dispatched input has a corresponding `batch-<batchIndex>.json` (or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-*.json`) on disk before proceeding to the next dispatch.

Run the merge-and-normalize script bundled with this skill (located next to this SKILL.md file — use the skill directory path, not the project root):
```bash
python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This script reads all `batch-*.json` files (including `batch-<i>-part-<k>.json` produced by file-analyzers that split their output) from `$UA_DIR/intermediate/`, then in one pass:
- Combines all nodes and edges across batches
- Normalizes node IDs (strips double prefixes, project-name prefixes, adds missing prefixes)
- Normalizes complexity values (`low`→`simple`, `medium`→`moderate`, `high`→`complex`, etc.)
- Rewrites edge references to match corrected node IDs
- Deduplicates nodes by ID (keeps last occurrence) and edges by `(source, target, type)`
- Drops dangling edges referencing missing nodes
- Logs all corrections and dropped items to stderr

The merge script also runs a `tested_by` linker that canonicalizes test-coverage edges in two passes. **Pass 1** walks LLM-emitted `tested_by` edges and flips inverted ones in place; semantically broken edges (test↔test, prod↔prod, orphan endpoints) are dropped. **Pass 2** supplements with path-convention pairings. Production nodes that end up sourcing any `tested_by` edge get a `"tested"` tag. All resulting edges run `production → test`.

Output: `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`

Include the script's warnings in `$PHASE_WARNINGS` for the reviewer.


This produces a `batches.json` that contains only batches with changed files, but neighborMap entries still reference unchanged files (with their full-graph batchIndex) so cross-batch edges remain emittable.

Then dispatch file-analyzer subagents per the same template as the full path.

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

Full reserve norm implementing round 4 policy.
Features:
- Per‑trip cap of 4 kg, with up to 1 kg kept for sustenance and the remainder deposited to a communal reserve.
- Tracks each fisher's total catch for the round (treated as a month).
- Enforces a monthly catch limit of 10 % of the lake biomass. Any excess is returned and double‑deposited as a penalty.
- Updates the communal reserve accordingly at round end.
- Emits notes via NormDecision and records sanctions in the norm state for further processing.
"""

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class FullReserveNorm(Norm):
    """Round 4 norm implementation.

    * Per‑trip: max 4 kg total, keep at most 1 kg, deposit rest to reserve.
    * Monthly: total catch may not exceed 10 % of lake biomass. Excess is returned
      and double‑deposited as a penalty.
    """

    type_name = "full_reserve"

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Apply per‑trip constraints and record raw catch.

        * Trim to 4 kg trip limit.
        * Compute kept (≤1 kg) and deposit to reserve.
        * Store the post‑cap raw catch in round‑scratch for monthly accounting.
        """
        note_parts = []
        # enforce absolute per‑trip cap
        if raw_kg > 4.0:
            raw_kg = 4.0
            note_parts.append("trimmed to 4 kg trip limit")

        # keep up to 1 kg, rest goes to reserve
        kept_kg = min(1.0, raw_kg)
        deposit_kg = raw_kg - kept_kg

        # persist reserve balance
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        state["reserve_kg"] = state.get("reserve_kg", 0.0) + deposit_kg

        if deposit_kg > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"deposited {deposit_kg:.2f} kg to communal reserve")

        # record raw catch for monthly limit checking
        monthly = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        monthly.setdefault("catch_by_agent", {})
        monthly["catch_by_agent"][agent_id] = (
            monthly["catch_by_agent"].get(agent_id, 0.0) + raw_kg
        )

        note = ", ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept_kg, note=note)

    def on_round_end(self, context, round_results):
        """Enforce monthly 10 % biomass cap.

        The lake biomass at the start of the round is available as
        ``context.stock_before``. If an agent's total catch exceeds 10 % of that
        biomass, the excess is considered returned and double‑deposited to the
        reserve. A sanction note is added to the norm state for each violator.
        """
        # monthly catch tracking stored in round‑scratch
        monthly = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        catch_by_agent = monthly.get("catch_by_agent", {})
        if not catch_by_agent:
            return None

        biomass_limit = 0.10 * context.stock_before
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        for agent_id, total_catch in catch_by_agent.items():
            if total_catch > biomass_limit:
                excess = total_catch - biomass_limit
                penalty = excess * 2.0
                # add penalty to reserve
                state["reserve_kg"] = state.get("reserve_kg", 0.0) + penalty
                # record a sanction for this agent
                sanctions = state.setdefault("sanctions", {})
                sanctions[agent_id] = {
                    "excess": excess,
                    "penalty_deposited": penalty,
                }
        return None

**Policy**
Each fisher may harvest up to **4 kg** per trip: **1 kg** for personal sustenance and **3 kg** deposited into a communal reserve. Monthly catch may not exceed **10 %** of the lake’s current biomass; any excess must be returned to the lake immediately and double‑deposited as a penalty. The reserve is released only when lake biomass falls below **80 kg** and after a **4‑month** refill period. Allocation of released reserves is decided by a rotating committee of three monitors who first aid fishers with the lowest balances, then proportionally share remaining reserves.

**Operationalization**
1. After each trip, the fisher records total catch in the communal ledger; **1 kg** is deducted for sustenance, the remainder (up to **3 kg**) is deposited into the communal reserve bin and logged.
2. The system tracks each fisher’s cumulative catch for the round (treated as a month). If a fisher’s total exceeds **10 %** of the lake’s current biomass, the excess weight is immediately returned to the lake and the fisher deposits double that amount into the reserve bin; this penalty is recorded and verified by two monitors.
3. Lake biomass is measured at the start of each round and logged.
4. When biomass drops below **80 kg** and a **4‑month** refill period (counted from the last reserve release date) has elapsed, a rotating committee of three impartial community monitors convenes.
5. The committee reviews the ledger for the period, calculates each fisher’s net balance (catch minus sustenance minus reserve deposits), identifies fishers with the lowest balances, and allocates reserve funds first to bring those balances to at least zero or a predefined sustainability threshold.
6. Any remaining reserve is divided proportionally among all fishers based on the amount each contributed to the reserve during the refill period.
7. All allocations, dates, and rationales are entered into the ledger; a summary is published to the community.
8. Fishers may submit a written request to the committee to review any allocation; the committee will re‑examine the ledger and make a final decision.

3: **Policy**
4: Each fisher may harvest up to **4 kg** per trip: **1 kg** for personal sustenance and **3 kg** deposited into a communal reserve. Monthly catch may not exceed **10 %** of the lake’s current biomass; any excess must be returned to the lake immediately and double‑deposited as a penalty. The reserve is released only when lake biomass falls below **80 kg** and after a **4‑month** refill period. Allocation of released reserves is decided by a rotating committee of three monitors who first aid fishers with the lowest balances, then proportionally share remaining reserves.
5: 
6: **Operationalization**
7: 1. After each trip, the fisher records total catch in the communal ledger; **1 kg** is deducted for sustenance, the remainder (up to **3 kg**) is deposited into the communal reserve bin and logged.
8: 2. The system tracks each fisher’s cumulative catch for the round (treated as a month). If a fisher’s total exceeds **10 %** of the lake’s current biomass, the excess weight is immediately returned to the lake and the fisher deposits double that amount into the reserve bin; this penalty is recorded and verified by two monitors.
9: 3. Lake biomass is measured at the start of each round and logged.
10: 4. When biomass drops below **80 kg** and a **4‑month** refill period (counted from the last reserve release date) has elapsed, a rotating committee of three impartial community monitors convenes.
11: 5. The committee reviews the ledger for the period, calculates each fisher’s net balance (catch minus sustenance minus reserve deposits), identifies fishers with the lowest balances, and allocates reserve funds first to bring those balances to at least zero or a predefined sustainability threshold.
12: 6. Any remaining reserve is divided proportionally among all fishers based on the amount each contributed to the reserve during the refill period.
13: 7. All allocations, dates, and rationales are entered into the ledger; a summary is published to the community.
14: 8. Fishers may submit a written request to the committee to review any allocation; the committee will re‑examine the ledger and make a final decision.

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision

    """Round 4 norm implementation.

    * Per‑trip: max 4 kg total, keep at most 1 kg, deposit rest to reserve.
    * Monthly: total catch may not exceed 10 % of lake biomass. Excess is returned
      and double‑deposited as a penalty.
    """

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Apply per‑trip constraints and record raw catch.

        * Trim to 4 kg trip limit.
        * Compute kept (≤1 kg) and deposit to reserve.
        * Store the post‑cap raw catch in round‑scratch for monthly accounting.
        """
        note_parts = []

        if raw_kg > 4.0:
            raw_kg = 4.0
            note_parts.append("trimmed to 4 kg trip limit")

        # keep up to 1 kg, rest goes to reserve
        kept_kg = min(1.0, raw_kg)
        deposit_kg = raw_kg - kept_kg

        # persist reserve balance
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        state["reserve_kg"] = state.get("reserve_kg", 0.0) + deposit_kg

        if deposit_kg > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"deposited {deposit_kg:.2f} kg to communal reserve")

        # record raw catch for monthly limit checking
        monthly = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        monthly.setdefault("catch_by_agent", {})
        monthly["catch_by_agent"][agent_id] = (
            monthly["catch_by_agent"].get(agent_id, 0.0) + raw_kg
        )

        note = ", ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept_kg, note=note)

    def on_round_end(self, context, round_results):
        """Enforce monthly 10 % biomass cap.

        The lake biomass at the start of the round is available as
        ``context.stock_before``. If an agent's total catch exceeds 10 % of that

        reserve. A sanction note is added to the norm state for each violator.
        """
        # monthly catch tracking stored in round‑scratch
        monthly = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        catch_by_agent = monthly.get("catch_by_agent", {})
        if not catch_by_agent:
            return None

        biomass_limit = 0.10 * context.stock_before
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        for agent_id, total_catch in catch_by_agent.items():
            if total_catch > biomass_limit:
                excess = total_catch - biomass_limit
                penalty = excess * 2.0
                # add penalty to reserve
                state["reserve_kg"] = state.get("reserve_kg", 0.0) + penalty
                # record a sanction for this agent
                sanctions = state.setdefault("sanctions", {})
                sanctions[agent_id] = {
                    "excess": excess,
                    "penalty_deposited": penalty,
                }

3: Operationalization: 1. I will keep the reserve bin and verify each 3 kg deposit, recording the amount, fisher name, trip date and ledger entry; I will also record any penalty deposits and the dates of releases. 2. After each trip, the communal scale will weigh the catch; the sustenance 1 kg will be deducted, and any remaining weight will be entered in the ledger as catch. 3. Monthly totals are summed per fisher; if a fisher’s total exceeds 10 % of the lake’s current biomass, the excess weight is returned to the lake immediately and the fisher deposits double that weight into the reserve bin, with the action recorded and verified by two monitors. 4. The lake biomass is measured each month and logged in the ledger. 5.     """With config["norms"] == [], HarvestAction.run() must be pure physics —

    expected_payoff_0 = apply_consumption(0.0, raw_0)

    assert state["runtime"]["payoff"]["agent_0"] == pytest.approx(expected_payoff_0)
    assert state["runtime"]["payoff"]["agent_1"] == pytest.approx(expected_payoff_1)
    assert state["runtime"]["dead_agents"] == []


def test_baseline_no_norm_state_key_created_when_norms_empty(monkeypatch):

```python
2	# norm type is exactly "add norms/<name>.py defining a Norm subclass with a

4	# file stay 100% denied to the norm-implementer forever (see
5	# .opencode/agent/norm-implementer.md's permission.edit) without that also
6	# blocking it from ever introducing a new norm type — the one thing a
7	# hand-maintained NORM_TYPES dict here would have required editing this
8	# denied file for.

10	import importlib
11	import pkgutil
12	
13	import norms as _norms_package
14	from engine.norms.base import Norm
15	
16	
17	def _discover_norm_types():
18	    types = {}
19	    for module_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(_norms_package.__path__, prefix="norms."):
20	        module = importlib.import_module(module_info.name)
21	        for attr in vars(module).values():
22	            if isinstance(attr, type) and issubclass(attr, Norm) and attr is not Norm and attr.type_name:
23	                existing = types.get(attr.type_name)
24	                if existing is not None and existing is not attr:
25	                    raise ValueError(
26	                        f"{module_info.name}: type_name {attr.type_name!r} is already "
27	                        f"registered by {existing.__module__} — norm type_names must be "
28	                        f"unique across norms/*.py"
29	                    )
30	                types[attr.type_name] = attr
31	    return types
32	
33	
34	NORM_TYPES = _discover_norm_types()

37	def load_norms(config):
38	    specs = config.get("norms", [])
39	    norms = []
40	    seen_keys = set()
41	    for i, spec in enumerate(specs):
42	        norm_type = spec.get("type")
43	        cls = NORM_TYPES.get(norm_type)
44	        if cls is None:
45	            raise ValueError(
46	                f"state/config.json norms[{i}]: unknown norm type {norm_type!r} — "
47	                f"must be one of {sorted(NORM_TYPES)}"
48	            )
49	        key = spec.get("id", norm_type)
50	        if key in seen_keys:
51	            raise ValueError(
52	                f"state/config.json norms[{i}]: duplicate norm key {key!r} — set an "
53	                f'explicit "id" to disambiguate multiple norms of the same type'
54	            )
55	        seen_keys.add(key)
56	        norms.append(cls(key=key, params=spec))
```

```python
4	# file stay 100% denied to the norm-implementer forever (see

6	# blocking it from ever introducing a new norm type — the one thing a
7	# hand-maintained NORM_TYPES dict here would have required editing this
8	# denied file for.

10	import importlib
11	import pkgutil
12	
13	import norms as _norms_package
14	from engine.norms.base import Norm
15	
16	
17	def _discover_norm_types():
18	    types = {}
19	    for module_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(_norms_package.__path__, prefix="norms."):
20	        module = importlib.import_module(module_info.name)
21	        for attr in vars(module).values():
22	            if isinstance(attr, type) and issubclass(attr, Norm) and attr is not Norm and attr.type_name:
23	                existing = types.get(attr.type_name)
24	                if existing is not None and existing is not attr:
25	                    raise ValueError(
26	                        f"{module_info.name}: type_name {attr.type_name!r} is already "
27	                        f"registered by {existing.__module__} — norm type_names must be "
28	                        f"unique across norms/*.py"
29	                    )
30	                types[attr.type_name] = attr
31	    return types
32	
33	
34	NORM_TYPES = _discover_norm_types()
35	
36	
37	def load_norms(config):
38	    specs = config.get("norms", [])
39	    norms = []
40	    seen_keys = set()
41	    for i, spec in enumerate(specs):
42	        norm_type = spec.get("type")
43	        cls = NORM_TYPES.get(norm_type)
44	        if cls is None:
45	            raise ValueError(
46	                f"state/config.json norms[{i}]: unknown norm type {norm_type!r} — "
47	                f"must be one of {sorted(NORM_TYPES)}"
48	            )
49	        key = spec.get("id", norm_type)
50	        if key in seen_keys:
51	            raise ValueError(
52	                f"state/config.json norms[{i}]: duplicate norm key {key!r} — set an "
53	                f'explicit "id" to disambiguate multiple norms of the same type'
54	            )
55	        seen_keys.add(key)
56	        norms.append(cls(key=key, params=spec))
57	    return norms
```

```python
11	@dataclass
12	class NormDecision:
13	    """The result of one norm's evaluate() call for one agent, or the final
14	    chained result of a whole round's NormEngine.apply(). kept_kg is the
15	    only field with unconditional meaning; note/sanction/violated are
16	    optional signals other norms (via engine chaining) and the round record
17	    (via results[agent_id]["note"]) can act on."""
18

20	    note: str | None = None
21	    sanction: str | None = None
22	    violated: bool = False
23	
24	    @classmethod
25	    def allow(cls, kept_kg):
26	        """No change — this norm has nothing to say about this catch."""
27	        return cls(kept_kg=kept_kg)
28	
29	    @classmethod
30	    def adjust(cls, kept_kg, note=None):
31	        """A non-punitive change to kept_kg (a reserve top-up, e.g.) —
32	        distinct from violation() so a round's outcome doesn't read as a
33	        sanction just because some norm touched the number."""
34	        return cls(kept_kg=kept_kg, note=note)
35

39	        etc. sanction is an opaque string another norm plugin can key its
40	        own escalating-consequence logic off (a ban that triggers after N
41	        matching sanctions, say) — not interpreted by the engine itself."""
42	        return cls(kept_kg=kept_kg, sanction=sanction, note=note, violated=True)
43

46	        """This agent gets nothing from this trip at all."""

52	    by engine.norms.registry.load_norms() — construction is cheap (just
53	    stores key/params); a norm never keeps state on self between calls,
54	    since a new instance exists every round. Cross-round-persistent state
55	    lives at context.norm_state(self.key) (backed by runtime["norms"][key],

63	        self.key = key
```

**Policy**
Each fisher may take up to **4 kg** per trip: **1 kg** is kept for personal sustenance and the remaining **3 kg** is deposited into a communal reserve. The reserve may be drawn only when lake biomass falls below **70 kg** **and** at least **six months** have elapsed since the last reserve release. No fisher’s **monthly total catch** may exceed **8 %** of the lake’s current biomass.

**Operationalization**
1. At the start of each calendar year a **communal steward** is elected by simple majority. The steward is responsible for maintaining the shared ledger, overseeing the reserve, and enforcing the policy.
2. After each trip the fisher records the **total catch** in the ledger. The steward automatically deducts **1 kg** for personal use and logs the **3 kg** deposit to the communal reserve.
3. The ledger tracks each fisher’s **cumulative catch for the month**. If a fisher’s monthly total exceeds **8 %** of the lake’s current biomass, the excess is **returned to the lake** and the fisher receives a **two‑month fishing suspension**; their gear is temporarily confiscated. The violation is recorded in the ledger along with the sanction.
4. Lake biomass is measured monthly by a rotating monitoring group using calibrated float methods; the current biomass value is stored as `context.stock_before` for the round.
5. When biomass drops below **70 kg** **and** at least **six months** have passed since the previous reserve release, the steward may **open the reserve**. While the reserve is open, no single trip may draw more than **3 kg** from the reserve until biomass rises above **70 kg** again.
6. All actions – election results, deposit records, quota calculations, forfeiture notices, and reserve releases – are entered into the shared ledger and displayed on the community warning board for full transparency.

**Operationalization**
1. At the start of each calendar year a **communal steward** is elected by simple majority. The steward is responsible for maintaining the shared ledger, overseeing the reserve, and enforcing the policy.
2. After each trip the fisher records the **total catch** in the ledger. The steward automatically deducts **1 kg** for personal use and logs the **3 kg** deposit to the communal reserve.
3. The ledger tracks each fisher’s **cumulative catch for the month**. If a fisher’s monthly total exceeds **8 %** of the lake’s current biomass, the excess is **returned to the lake** and the fisher receives a **two‑month fishing suspension**; their gear is temporarily confiscated. The violation is recorded in the ledger along with the sanction.
4. Lake biomass is measured monthly by a rotating monitoring group using calibrated float methods; the current biomass value is stored as `context.stock_before` for the round.
5. When biomass drops below **70 kg** **and** at least **six months** have passed since the previous reserve release, the steward may **open the reserve**. While the reserve is open, no single trip may draw more than **3 kg** from the reserve until biomass rises above **70 kg** again.

Features:
- Per‑trip cap of 4 kg, with up to 1 kg kept for sustenance and the remainder deposited to a communal reserve.

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class FullReserveNorm(Norm):
    """Round 4 norm implementation.

    * Per‑trip: max 4 kg total, keep at most 1 kg, deposit rest to reserve.
    * Monthly: total catch may not exceed 10 % of lake biomass. Excess is returned
      and double‑deposited as a penalty.
    """

    type_name = "full_reserve"

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Apply per‑trip constraints and record raw catch.

        * Trim to 4 kg trip limit.
        * Compute kept (≤1 kg) and deposit to reserve.
        * Store the post‑cap raw catch in round‑scratch for monthly accounting.
        """
        note_parts = []
        # enforce absolute per‑trip cap
        if raw_kg > 4.0:
            raw_kg = 4.0
            note_parts.append("trimmed to 4 kg trip limit")

        # keep up to 1 kg, rest goes to reserve
        kept_kg = min(1.0, raw_kg)
        deposit_kg = raw_kg - kept_kg

        # persist reserve balance
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        state["reserve_kg"] = state.get("reserve_kg", 0.0) + deposit_kg

        if deposit_kg > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"deposited {deposit_kg:.2f} kg to communal reserve")

        # record raw catch for monthly limit checking
        monthly = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        monthly.setdefault("catch_by_agent", {})
        monthly["catch_by_agent"][agent_id] = (
            monthly["catch_by_agent"].get(agent_id, 0.0) + raw_kg
        )

        note = ", ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept_kg, note=note)

    def on_round_end(self, context, round_results):
        """Enforce monthly 10 % biomass cap.

        The lake biomass at the start of the round is available as
        ``context.stock_before``. If an agent's total catch exceeds 10 % of that
        biomass, the excess is considered returned and double‑deposited to the
        reserve. A sanction note is added to the norm state for each violator.
        """
        # monthly catch tracking stored in round‑scratch
        monthly = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        catch_by_agent = monthly.get("catch_by_agent", {})
        if not catch_by_agent:
            return None

        biomass_limit = 0.10 * context.stock_before
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        for agent_id, total_catch in catch_by_agent.items():
            if total_catch > biomass_limit:
                excess = total_catch - biomass_limit
                penalty = excess * 2.0
                # add penalty to reserve
                state["reserve_kg"] = state.get("reserve_kg", 0.0) + penalty
                # record a sanction for this agent
                sanctions = state.setdefault("sanctions", {})
                sanctions[agent_id] = {
                    "excess": excess,
                    "penalty_deposited": penalty,
                }

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

## Phase 0 — Pre-flight

Determine whether to run a full analysis or incremental update.

1. **Resolve `PROJECT_ROOT`:**
   - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for a non-flag token (any argument that does not start with `--`). If found, treat it as the target directory path.
     - If the path is relative, resolve it against the current working directory.
     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.
     - Set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the resolved absolute path.
   - If no directory path argument is found, set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the current working directory.
   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).
1.5. **Ensure the plugin is built.** Later phases invoke Node scripts that import `@understand-anything/core`. On a fresh install `packages/core/dist/` does not exist yet — build once.

   **Important:** do **not** assume the plugin root is simply two directories above the skill path string. In many installations `~/.agents/skills/understand` is a symlink into the real plugin checkout. Prefer runtime-provided plugin roots first (for Claude), then fall back to universal symlinks, skill symlink resolution, and common clone-based install paths.

   Resolve the plugin root like this:

   ```bash
   SKILL_REAL=$(realpath ~/.agents/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || readlink -f ~/.agents/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   SELF_RELATIVE=$([ -n "$SKILL_REAL" ] && cd "$SKILL_REAL/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")
   COPILOT_SKILL_REAL=$(realpath ~/.copilot/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || readlink -f ~/.copilot/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE=$([ -n "$COPILOT_SKILL_REAL" ] && cd "$COPILOT_SKILL_REAL/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")

   PLUGIN_ROOT=""
   for candidate in \
     "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" \
     "$HOME/.understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"; do
     if [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate/package.json" ] && [ -f "$candidate/pnpm-workspace.yaml" ]; then
       PLUGIN_ROOT="$candidate"
       break
     fi
   done

   if [ -z "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ]; then
     echo "Error: Cannot find the understand-anything plugin root."
     echo "Checked:"
     echo "  - ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-<unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - ${SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.agents/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - ${COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.copilot/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "Make sure the plugin is installed correctly."
     exit 1
   fi

   if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_ROOT/packages/core/dist/index.js" ]; then
     cd "$PLUGIN_ROOT" && (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 2>/dev/null || pnpm install) && pnpm --filter @understand-anything/core build
   fi
   ```

   If `pnpm` is missing, report to the user: "Install Node.js ≥ 22 and pnpm ≥ 10, then re-run `/understand`."

1.7. **Resolve the data directory `$UA_DIR`.** All Understand-Anything artifacts live in the project's data directory. Resolve it once, now that `$PROJECT_ROOT` is known, and reuse `$UA_DIR` for every read and write in later phases:
   ```bash
   UA_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/$([ -d "$PROJECT_ROOT/.understand-anything" ] && echo .understand-anything || echo .ua)"
   ```
   This keeps the legacy `.understand-anything/` directory when it already exists (existing projects keep working with no migration) and uses the new `.ua/` otherwise. Because each phase may run in a fresh shell, treat `$UA_DIR` — like `$PROJECT_ROOT` — as a value you carry forward and substitute; re-resolve it with the line above if a later command block needs it in a new shell.

2. Get the current git commit hash:

3. Create the intermediate and temp output directories:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p "$UA_DIR/intermediate"
   mkdir -p "$UA_DIR/tmp"
   ```

3.1. **Purge stale trash dirs.** Phase 7 cleanup `mv`s scratch dirs into `.trash-<timestamp>/` rather than `rm -rf`ing them directly (see issue #301), so that destructive-action gates on hardened hosts don't trip on just-created paths. Reclaim the space here once the trash is older than 7 days — by this point any freshness-window check has long since stopped caring about those dirs:
   ```bash
   find "$UA_DIR/" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '.trash-*' -mtime +7 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
   ```
3.5. **Auto-update configuration:**
    - If `--auto-update` is in `$ARGUMENTS`: write `{"autoUpdate": true}` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`
    - If `--no-auto-update` is in `$ARGUMENTS`: write `{"autoUpdate": false}` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`
    - These flags only set the config — analysis proceeds normally regardless.

 3.6. **Language configuration:**
    - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for `--language <lang>` flag. If found, extract the language code.
    - **Language code normalization:** Map friendly names to ISO codes:
      - `chinese` → `zh`, `japanese` → `ja`, `korean` → `ko`, `english` → `en`, `spanish` → `es`, `french` → `fr`, `german` → `de`, `portuguese` → `pt`, `russian` → `ru`, `arabic` → `ar`, etc.
      - Locale variants: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-CN`, `pt-BR`, etc. are preserved as-is.
    - If `--language` is NOT specified:
      - **Stored preference wins.** If `$UA_DIR/config.json` has an `outputLanguage` field, set `$OUTPUT_LANGUAGE` to it and skip the rest.
      - **Otherwise detect (first run only).** Infer the predominant language of the user's conversation as an ISO 639-1 code (`$DETECTED_LANG`). If it is `en` or cannot be confidently determined, set `$OUTPUT_LANGUAGE=en` and proceed silently — no prompt (English users see no change).
      - **If `$DETECTED_LANG` ≠ `en`, confirm once before analyzing:** tell the user you detected `<language>` and ask whether to generate all content in it; they press Enter/"yes" to accept, or type another language code/name to override (normalize via the friendly-name map above). If running non-interactively (no reply possible), skip the wait, use `$DETECTED_LANG`, and print a one-line notice instead of blocking.
      - **Persist** the resolved `$OUTPUT_LANGUAGE` (including `en`) into `config.json` so it never re-prompts for this project.
    - If `--language` IS specified:
      - Update `$UA_DIR/config.json` with the new language: merge `{"outputLanguage": "<lang>"}` into existing config.
      - Store as `$OUTPUT_LANGUAGE` for use throughout all phases.
    - **Language directive template:** Store as `$LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE`:
      ```markdown
      > **Language directive**: Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in **{language}**. Maintain technical accuracy while using natural, native-level phrasing in the target language. Keep technical terms in English when no standard translation exists (e.g., "middleware", "hook", "barrel").
      ```

 3.7. **Exclude patterns:**
    - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for `--exclude <patterns>` flag. If found, extract the comma-separated patterns string.
    - Split on commas, trim whitespace from each pattern, and filter out empty entries.
    - Store the patterns as `$EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (comma-joined for passing to downstream scripts: `"tests/*,docs/*"`).
    - These patterns take highest priority — they are applied on top of default patterns and `.understandignore` rules. Use `!` prefix to force-include files that would otherwise be excluded.
    - **Note:** Newly added `--exclude` patterns require a `--full` scan to take effect.

4. **Check for subdomain knowledge graphs to merge:**
   List all `*knowledge-graph*.json` files in `$UA_DIR/` **excluding** `knowledge-graph.json` itself (e.g. `frontend-knowledge-graph.json`, `backend-knowledge-graph.json`). If any subdomain graphs exist, run the merge script bundled with this skill (located next to this SKILL.md file — use the skill directory path, not the project root):
   ```bash
   python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-subdomain-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
   ```
   The script discovers subdomain graphs, loads the existing `knowledge-graph.json` as a base (if present), and merges everything into `knowledge-graph.json` (deduplicating nodes and edges). Report the merge summary to the user, then continue with the merged graph.

5. Check if `$UA_DIR/knowledge-graph.json` exists. If it does, read it.
6. Check if `$UA_DIR/meta.json` exists. If it does, read it to get `gitCommitHash`.
7. **Decision logic:**

   | Condition | Action |
   |---|---|
   | `--full` flag in `$ARGUMENTS` | Full analysis (all phases) |
   | No existing graph or meta | Full analysis (all phases) |
   | `--review` flag + existing graph + unchanged commit hash | Skip to Phase 6 (review-only — reuse existing assembled graph) |
   | Existing graph + unchanged commit hash | Ask the user: "The graph is up to date at this commit. Would you like to: **(a)** run a full rebuild (`--full`), **(b)** run the LLM graph reviewer (`--review`), or **(c)** do nothing?" Then follow their choice. If they pick (c), STOP. |
   | Existing graph + changed files | Incremental update (re-analyze changed files only) |

   **Review-only path:** Copy the existing `knowledge-graph.json` to `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`, then jump directly to Phase 6 step 3.

   For incremental updates, get the changed file list:
   ```bash
   git diff <lastCommitHash>..HEAD --name-only
   ```
   If this returns no files, report "Graph is up to date" and STOP.

8. **Collect project context for subagent injection:**
   - Read `README.md` (or `README.rst`, `readme.md`) from `$PROJECT_ROOT` if it exists. Store as `$README_CONTENT` (first 3000 characters).
   - Read the primary package manifest (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `pom.xml`) if it exists. Store as `$MANIFEST_CONTENT`.
   - Capture the top-level directory tree:
     ```bash
     find "$PROJECT_ROOT" -maxdepth 2 -type f -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -path '*/.git/*' -not -path '*/dist/*' | head -100
     ```
     Store as `$DIR_TREE`.
   - Detect the project entry point by checking for common patterns (in order): `src/index.ts`, `src/main.ts`, `src/App.tsx`, `index.js`, `main.py`, `manage.py`, `app.py`, `wsgi.py`, `asgi.py`, `run.py`, `__main__.py`, `main.go`, `cmd/*/main.go`, `src/main.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/main/java/**/Application.java`, `Program.cs`, `config.ru`, `index.php`. Store first match as `$ENTRY_POINT`.

## Phase 2 — ANALYZE

### Full analysis path

Load `$UA_DIR/intermediate/batches.json` (produced by Phase 1.5). Iterate the `batches[]` array.

Report: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files — <totalFiles> files in <totalBatches> batches (up to 5 concurrent)...`

For each batch, dispatch a subagent using the `file-analyzer` agent definition (at `agents/file-analyzer.md`). Run up to **5 subagents concurrently**. Append the following additional context:

> **Additional context from main session:**
>
> Project: `<projectName>` — `<projectDescription>`
> Languages: `<languages from Phase 1>`
>
> $LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE

Dispatch prompt template (fill in batch-specific values from `batches.json[i]`):

> Analyze these files and produce GraphNode and GraphEdge objects.
> Project root: `$PROJECT_ROOT`
> Project: `<projectName>`
> Languages: `<languages>`
> Batch: `<batchIndex>/<totalBatches>`
> Skill directory (for bundled scripts): `<SKILL_DIR>`
> Output: write to `$UA_DIR/intermediate/batch-<batchIndex>.json` (single-file mode) OR `batch-<batchIndex>-part-<k>.json` (split mode, per Step B of your output protocol).
>
> Pre-resolved import data for this batch (use directly — do NOT re-resolve imports from source):
> ```json
> <batchImportData JSON from batches.json[i].batchImportData>
> ```
>
> Cross-batch neighbors with their exported symbols (confidence boost for cross-batch edges):
> ```json
> <neighborMap JSON from batches.json[i].neighborMap>
> ```
>
> Files to analyze in this batch (every entry MUST be passed through to `batchFiles` with all four fields — `path`, `language`, `sizeLines`, `fileCategory`):
> 1. `<path>` (<sizeLines> lines, language: `<language>`, fileCategory: `<fileCategory>`)
> 2. `<path>` (<sizeLines> lines, language: `<language>`, fileCategory: `<fileCategory>`)
> ...

**Output naming is per-batchIndex — no fusion.** If you fuse multiple small batches into a single file-analyzer dispatch for token efficiency, the dispatched agent must STILL write one output file per original `batchIndex` using `batch-<batchIndex>.json` or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-<k>.json`. The merge script's regex (`batch-(\d+)(?:-part-(\d+))?\.json`) silently drops any other naming (e.g., `batch-fused-8-13.json`, `batch-8-13.json`), losing every node and edge in that file. After each dispatch returns, verify each `batchIndex` in the dispatched input has a corresponding `batch-<batchIndex>.json` (or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-*.json`) on disk before proceeding to the next dispatch.

After ALL batches complete, report to the user: `Phase 2 complete. All <totalBatches> batches analyzed.`

Run the merge-and-normalize script bundled with this skill (located next to this SKILL.md file — use the skill directory path, not the project root):
```bash
python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This script reads all `batch-*.json` files (including `batch-<i>-part-<k>.json` produced by file-analyzers that split their output) from `$UA_DIR/intermediate/`, then in one pass:
- Combines all nodes and edges across batches
- Normalizes node IDs (strips double prefixes, project-name prefixes, adds missing prefixes)
- Normalizes complexity values (`low`→`simple`, `medium`→`moderate`, `high`→`complex`, etc.)
- Rewrites edge references to match corrected node IDs
- Deduplicates nodes by ID (keeps last occurrence) and edges by `(source, target, type)`
- Drops dangling edges referencing missing nodes
- Logs all corrections and dropped items to stderr

The merge script also runs a `tested_by` linker that canonicalizes test-coverage edges in two passes. **Pass 1** walks LLM-emitted `tested_by` edges and flips inverted ones in place; semantically broken edges (test↔test, prod↔prod, orphan endpoints) are dropped. **Pass 2** supplements with path-convention pairings. Production nodes that end up sourcing any `tested_by` edge get a `"tested"` tag. All resulting edges run `production → test`.

Output: `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`

Include the script's warnings in `$PHASE_WARNINGS` for the reviewer.

### Incremental update path

Write the changed-files list (one path per line) to a temp file:
```bash
git diff "<lastCommitHash>..HEAD" --name-only > "$UA_DIR/tmp/changed-files.txt"
```

Run compute-batches with `--changed-files`:
```bash
node "<SKILL_DIR>/compute-batches.mjs" "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --changed-files="$UA_DIR/tmp/changed-files.txt"
```

This produces a `batches.json` that contains only batches with changed files, but neighborMap entries still reference unchanged files (with their full-graph batchIndex) so cross-batch edges remain emittable.

Then dispatch file-analyzer subagents per the same template as the full path.

After batches complete:
1. Remove old nodes whose `filePath` matches any changed file from the existing graph
2. Remove old edges whose `source` or `target` references a removed node
3. Write the pruned existing nodes/edges as `batch-existing.json` in the intermediate directory
4. Run the same merge script — it will combine `batch-existing.json` with the fresh `batch-*.json` files:
   ```bash
   python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
   ```

## Phase 3 — ASSEMBLE REVIEW

Report to the user: `[Phase 3/7] Reviewing assembled graph...`
